Will continue to bid for tournament in the coming months. Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum monthly attendance for December was 1,635. This number includes: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visitation includes 498 walk-in guests and 565 visitors to special events, meetings, tours, etc. In addition to Arkansas, visitors have come from 21 states, including Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia, as well as Australia, Mexico, and Germany. Off-site programming reached a total of 275 individuals during December, while the museum's virtual programming received 297 new views. Overall attendance thus far in 2025 totals 6 35,403, which is 102% of the museum's goal. During 2025, a total of 17,834 guests participated in onsite visitation and special events (50%), 5,974 views of virtual programming (17%) and 11,595 reached through off-site outreach and programming (33%). The museum received $11,038.50 in donations in December, including $10,210 in sponsorships for the Thomas Hart Benton exhibit. Total fundraising for 2025 was $63,575: this amount more than doubles the annual goal of raising $30,000. Since 2016 the museum has raised over $612,500 in outside funding through grants, sponsorships and donations. Gift shop sales for the year were $12,327.31, exceeding the 2025 goal by 8% and setting a record for highest gift shop sales in a single year since the museum opened in 2001. So far this Fall, a total of 1077 students have been reached at the sites: (1) Dunbar Community Center – 534, (2) Stephens Community Center – 391, and (3) J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy – 152. Thomas Hart Benton, a traveling exhibit from the Naval History and Heritage Command in Washington DC, continues to receive favorable response from the public. It features 25 original paintings and drawings depicting naval scenes on board the submarine USS Dorado and LSTs along the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers. These artworks were commissioned by Abbott Laboratories and turned over to the Navy after the war. The exhibit will remain on display through July 31. The museum hosted three holiday concerts during December. Forty-four people attended the concert of the 106th Army Band's "Low Brass" ensemble group on December 6. Thirty persons attended the “Jazz, Jingles and Joy,” concert featuring the Jacksonville High School Choir on December 13. Fortythree people attended the annual holiday concert featuring students from the Margaret Wyatt Piano and Vocal Studio on December 21. The museum’s “Movies at MacArthur” film series resumes in January, which marks the program’s twelfth year. Since starting in 2015, a total of 3,918 people has attended one or more screenings of movies depicting various topics in our state and nation’s military history.
